canice_verger.text: Welcome to St Canice's. Kilkenny comes from Cill Chainnigh, which means the church of Cainnech, or Canice. This is his hill.
Canice was a monk who lived in the 500s and knew Saint Columba. The cathedral you see is mostly from the 1200s.
It is one of the longest cathedrals in Ireland. The round tower beside it is older still. Climb it if your knees agree.

then.text: Mooney, verger. Yes, that's my cloak, yes, it's muddy, and yes, I was outside Kyteler's at midnight.
Petronilla de Meath was burnt in Kilkenny in 1324, and nobody has said a word for her since. So every year I light a candle on the inn step. I did not touch any pot.

else.text: Lovely old building, this. Ask me again if you ever hear there's trouble.
